story: A proud North London club with a history of attractive football and major honours. Management brings ambitious supporters, fierce local rivalries and the expectation of competing near the top.
challenge: Challenge for the league title while maintaining a fluent attacking style.

story: A south-coast club whose rise through the leagues gives its top-flight journey an underdog character. Managing the Cherries means building carefully and competing against clubs with greater resources.
challenge: Keep Bournemouth competitive in the Premier League and build for stability.

story: A Lancashire club with deep roots and a traditional home at Turf Moor. The job calls for organisation, resourcefulness and a team ready to compete against wealthier rivals.
challenge: Secure Premier League survival and make Turf Moor a difficult destination.

story: A London heavyweight with a taste for domestic and European silverware. At Stamford Bridge, the manager inherits high expectations and a squad expected to compete for major prizes.
challenge: Compete for the league title and pursue trophies on multiple fronts.

story: South London pride and the atmosphere at Selhurst Park shape this club's identity. The challenge is to channel that energy into consistent results against demanding Premier League opposition.
challenge: Establish a reliable league position and give supporters a cup run.

story: A historic Liverpool club with a proud league tradition and passionate supporters at Goodison Park. Managers face the challenge of turning that heritage into sustained competition near the top.
challenge: Push toward European qualification and make Goodison Park a fortress.

story: The Tigers represent Hull with an unmistakable black-and-amber identity. A Premier League campaign demands smart recruitment, collective resilience and points gathered wherever opportunities present themselves.
challenge: Keep Hull in the Premier League and strengthen the squad gradually.

story: The Foxes enter the era as reigning Premier League champions after a remarkable underdog triumph. Managing Leicester means embracing that spirit while meeting sharply raised expectations.
challenge: Remain competitive near the top and build on a historic title.

story: Anfield and a rich history of domestic and European success make this one of football's great stages. The manager must match passionate expectations with a team capable of challenging.
challenge: Challenge for the league title and pursue another memorable European campaign.

story: A Manchester club with modern title-winning ambition and considerable attacking expectations. The job calls for sustained excellence in the league and a credible pursuit of European honours.
challenge: Compete for the Premier League title and make a deep European run.

story: Old Trafford houses a club associated with major trophies, attacking football and enormous expectations. Managing United means restoring a consistent title challenge while embracing its demanding history.
challenge: Challenge for major trophies and return United to the league summit.

story: A Teesside club with a proud local following and a return to the Premier League. The task is to build a resilient side capable of holding its own.
challenge: Establish top-flight safety and build a foundation for future progress.

story: The Saints are known for developing talent and building competitive teams on the south coast. Management means balancing smart recruitment with ambitions to climb the Premier League table.
challenge: Develop young talent and pursue a place in the European positions.

story: A club rooted in the Potteries, Stoke brings a strong local identity and an established Premier League presence. The manager's challenge is to blend resilience with attacking progress.
challenge: Secure a comfortable league finish and push toward the top half.

story: The Black Cats bring a passionate Wearside following and a proud footballing history to the Stadium of Light. The immediate task is to create stability in a demanding league.
challenge: Secure Premier League survival and give the squad a steadier foundation.

story: A Welsh club competing in the English league system, Swansea carries a strong local identity. Management means preserving a competitive top-flight side while playing to its footballing strengths.
challenge: Stay in the Premier League and build a consistent attacking team.

story: A North London club with a tradition of ambitious, attacking football and a fiercely followed local rivalry. Managing Spurs means turning an exciting side into a trophy contender.
challenge: Challenge for the league title and bring silverware to North London.

story: The Hornets bring a compact home ground and a determined identity to the Premier League. The job is to forge consistency against opponents with a range of resources.
challenge: Keep Watford in the top flight and target a comfortable finish.

story: A historic West Midlands club with deep local roots and a long-established home at The Hawthorns. The manager must turn organisation and resolve into a dependable league campaign.
challenge: Secure a comfortable Premier League finish and compete strongly in cups.

story: The Hammers carry a proud East London identity and a reputation for developing talent. A new home brings fresh possibilities alongside supporters' familiar demands for entertaining football.
challenge: Build a competitive side in the new stadium and pursue Europe.

story: A Basque club with a loyal following at Mendizorrotza, Alavés return to the top flight for this campaign. Management calls for discipline and resourceful performances against larger clubs.
challenge: Establish LaLiga survival and make Mendizorrotza a challenging away trip.

story: Athletic's Basque player policy and passionate San Mamés support make this a distinctive managerial assignment. Success depends on developing eligible talent and maintaining the club's competitive traditions.
challenge: Develop eligible talent and challenge for European qualification and domestic cups.

story: A Madrid club known for fierce commitment, defensive strength and recent title contention. At the Vicente Calderón, expectations include challenging elite rivals at home and in Europe.
challenge: Challenge for LaLiga and sustain a strong run in European competition.

story: A global club with a deep commitment to possession football, academy development and major trophies. At Camp Nou, a manager must combine an attractive style with relentless results.
challenge: Win LaLiga while competing for the biggest domestic and European trophies.

story: Galician pride and the atmosphere at Balaídos give Celta a distinctive identity. The manager's task is to build an expressive, competitive side capable of challenging established LaLiga rivals.
challenge: Push for European places and give Vigo a strong cup campaign.

story: Dépor bring Galician pride and the memory of a league title to Riazor. Managing the club means honouring that history while building a stable, competitive top-flight team.
challenge: Secure a comfortable league finish and rebuild toward the top half.

story: A small Basque club competing against far larger LaLiga institutions, Eibar make resourcefulness a defining feature. At Ipurua, every point helps reinforce a remarkable top-flight foothold.
challenge: Keep Eibar in LaLiga and compete bravely against bigger clubs.

story: Barcelona's other major club brings a proud identity and a fierce local rivalry. Managing Espanyol means building a side that can compete consistently and give its supporters something to celebrate.
challenge: Aim for the top half and make a meaningful domestic cup run.

story: Granada represent an Andalusian city with devoted support at Los Cármenes. The challenge is to establish consistency and gather the points needed to compete in the top flight.
challenge: Secure LaLiga safety and build a more settled, competitive squad.

story: The Canary Islands club brings a distinctive island identity and a tradition of technical football. Managing Las Palmas means making home advantage count while navigating a demanding league.
challenge: Stay clear of relegation and develop an attractive, competitive side.

story: A club from the Madrid region beginning its first top-flight campaign, Leganés embody an underdog spirit. Success starts with organisation, resilience and strong performances at Butarque.
challenge: Keep Leganés in LaLiga and establish a platform for future seasons.

story: Málaga bring Andalusian character and a loyal following to La Rosaleda. The manager must build a consistent team and give supporters reason to dream beyond survival.
challenge: Earn a secure league finish and push toward the top half.

story: A Navarre club with a fiercely loyal following at El Sadar, Osasuna return to LaLiga with a clear challenge. Build a resilient side and make home matches count.
challenge: Secure top-flight safety and turn El Sadar into a dependable stronghold.

story: Betis bring green-and-white colours, passionate Seville support and a fierce city rivalry. Managing the club means matching that energy with consistent performances and ambitions beyond the lower half.
challenge: Push into the top half and make a strong cup challenge.

story: At the Santiago Bernabéu, a club steeped in domestic and European success demands major trophies. The manager is expected to combine star quality with consistent winning football.
challenge: Compete for LaLiga and the Champions League while meeting immense expectations.

story: A Basque club with a proud regional identity and a tradition of developing talent. The job is to build an attractive side capable of challenging for European places.
challenge: Develop promising players and compete for a European qualification place.

story: Sevilla combine an intense home atmosphere with a distinguished record in European competition. Managing the club means pursuing domestic progress and maintaining its appetite for continental success.
challenge: Challenge near the top of LaLiga and compete strongly in Europe.

story: A historic Asturian club with passionate support at El Molinón, Sporting carry a strong local identity. Their manager must build resilience against the pressures of top-flight football.
challenge: Keep Sporting in LaLiga and make home support count for points.

story: A club with major domestic and European pedigree, Valencia bring demanding expectations to Mestalla. Management means restoring consistency and giving a passionate fanbase a team to believe in.
challenge: Rebuild a consistent side and challenge for European qualification again.

story: The Yellow Submarine bring a distinctive identity and European ambition from a small city. Managing Villarreal means combining smart recruitment with a competitive, technically accomplished team.
challenge: Sustain a European challenge and remain competitive against larger LaLiga clubs.
